title: Brush Up: The 5-Minute Daily News - AI/Tech, Biz, World
description: Your definitive morning intelligence download. Every day shortly after 7:00 AM EST, we bypass the noise to deliver the critical shifts in AI, Global Business, and Macroeconomics that define the modern landscape. Brush up on the news while you brush up your smile.
latestSummary:
AI investment continues to surge, with Cohere’s new multilingual models and Ricursive Intelligence’s $335 million raise highlighting the sector’s dynamism. Venture capital firms are aggressively pursuing European AI startups, particularly those focused on specialized AI chips and computing architectures. However, Fractal Analytics’ underwhelming IPO signals investor caution regarding immediate AI financial returns. The ongoing India AI Impact Summit is attracting major tech players like OpenAI and Nvidia, emphasizing India’s push for domestic AI infrastructure and responsible development.

Stock market futures are declining due to concerns about AI disruption. Apple is preparing to unveil a more affordable iPhone, while Volkswagen announced a 20% cost reduction target by 2028 to address market pressures.

Geopolitically, talks between Russia and Ukraine remain stalled amidst continued military action. New nuclear talks between the United States and Iran are underway, coinciding with a US military buildup near Iran. China’s economic pressure on Japan, including recalling pandas and canceling flights, represents an escalation in tensions between the two nations.

title: Overnight Market Brief - Bridging the Global Gap. Daily.
description:
While North America sleeps, the global economy keeps moving. Overnight Market Brief is your essential pre-market digest, designed for traders, serious investors, and professionals who need to hit the ground running.
Most North American investors miss 50% of the market story because it happens in Tokyo, Hong Kong, and London. We bridge that gap. Every morning at 8:00 AM ET, we deliver a concise, data-driven breakdown and full global picture in under 10 minutes, just in time for your morning commute.
latestSummary:
Wall Street opened defensively on Friday, February 13, 2026, with the S&P 500 down 1.57% and the Nasdaq 100 declining 2.04% following a strong jobs report and risk-off sentiment. The 10-Year Treasury Yield rose to 4.102%, while the US Dollar Index increased to 96.93, and crude oil decreased to 62.61. Gold experienced a slight increase, reflecting safe-haven demand.

Overnight, Asian markets mirrored this weakness, with the Nikkei 225 down 1.21% and the Hang Seng and Shanghai Composite falling 1.72% and 1.26% respectively, driven by concerns about China’s economic health. European markets continued this trend, providing a weak lead-in for US traders.

US futures reflected this cautious sentiment, with S&P 500 futures down 0.24% and Nasdaq 100 futures down 0.29%. Investors are anticipating upcoming US CPI data, the evolving US Dollar positioning, and continued monitoring of China’s housing market data, which is expected to influence Federal Reserve policy and global growth sentiment. The market’s path of least resistance appears to be lower.

title: Post-market Recap
description:
Did the market "rally into the close" or "fade the open"? The Post-Market Recap goes beyond the green and red arrows to analyze the structure of the trading day. This daily briefing dissects the inter-market correlations that drove the session.
Every afternoon, we cover:
Macro Causality: Connecting the dots between the 10-Year Yield, the Dollar Index, and Equities.
Tech & AI Pulse: A dedicated segment on the semiconductor ecosystem and Big Tech performance.
Market Breadth: Analyzing Volatility (VIX) and Sector Rotation to gauge genuine institutional sentiment.
Closing Catalysts: Identifying the specific news and data that triggered late-day reversals.
latestSummary:
The Post-Market Recap for February 13, 2026, reveals a nuanced trading session marked by sector rotation and cautious investor sentiment. The S&P 500 gained 0.05%, closing at 6836.17, while the Nasdaq 100 rose 0.18% to 24732.73 and the Dow Jones increased by 49 points to 49500.93. Elevated trading volume indicated conviction behind repositioning, largely driven by the cooler-than-expected January Consumer Price Index, which rose 2.4% year-on-year.

This data eased pressure on bond yields and fueled a notable surge in the Utilities sector (XLU), up 2.76%, contrasting sharply with a modest gain for the Technology Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLK) and pullbacks in leading tech names like Nvidia (-2.23%) and Apple (-2.26%). Investors favored safety and defensive plays, suggesting a cautious approach to high-growth tech.

The US Dollar Index declined 0.07% to 96.77, reflecting reduced inflation expectations and a potentially less hawkish Federal Reserve. Crude Oil rose 0.08% to $62.89. Despite the overall market’s slight upward drift, the Magnificent Seven experienced significant pressure, indicating profit-taking or a rotation out of high-valuation growth stocks. The after-hours session saw notable gains in specific companies, highlighting continued market volatility. Investors are advised to carefully assess portfolio exposure and monitor geopolitical developments and commodity prices as they prepare for tomorrow’s trading.

title: Geopolitical Updates
description: Beyond the headlines lies strategy. Geopolitical Updates is your daily guide to the evolving global order. Each episode provides a rapid scan of the day's top international stories, followed by a deep-dive analysis of the single most impactful event shifting the geopolitical landscape. From tension in the South China Sea to economic statecraft in Europe, we explain not just what happened today, but why it matters for tomorrow. Delivered daily at 7 PM ET.
latestSummary:
Tensions in the Persian Gulf escalated as the U.S. Navy’s aircraft carrier group, including the USS Abraham Lincoln, approached Iranian waters ahead of planned talks between Washington and Tehran. This deployment, observed by BBC Verify, raises concerns about the diplomatic process and potential escalation.

In Eastern Europe, Lyudmila Navalnaya publicly asserted her belief that her son, Alexei Navalny, was murdered, reigniting calls for an international investigation. Across the Black Sea, Ukraine’s former energy minister was detained, continuing efforts to combat corruption and secure international support.

South America faces continued challenges with Venezuela’s political prisoners, complicating diplomatic efforts. In Kenya, airport delays due to labor disputes highlight infrastructure vulnerabilities. Israeli-Hamas tensions remain a concern, with police assisting after an incident involving ultra-Orthodox men.

The U.S.’s unverified deployment of the Abraham Lincoln group is strategically significant, potentially acting as a deterrent or bolstering the U.S. negotiating position. This heightened military presence could trigger a reactive posture from Iran, increasing the risk of miscalculation and further destabilizing the region’s already complex security landscape.
